entry_context_evidence.source_assertion: In MG-induced MC4100, Results reports weak uptake inhibition by glucose, mannose and mannitol, a smaller effect from trehalose, and none from fructose.
entry_context_evidence.source_locator: Author-uploaded full text retained web observation, lines L1323–L1354; JBC279:5537–5548

entry_context_evidence.source_assertion: No uptake inhibition was observed for maltose, arabinose, gluconate, glycerate, 1-alpha-glucosylglycerol, 2-alpha-glucosylglycerate or 2-alpha-mannosylglycerol in the reported MC4100 comparisons.
entry_context_evidence.source_locator: Author-uploaded full text retained web observation, lines L1350–L1372; JBC279:5537–5548

entry_context_evidence.source_assertion: Discussion reports no significant inhibition by mannose or the three named glycosyl analogues at 1 mM against 0.1 micromolar labeled MG. This contrasts with the weak mannose effect in Results; a direct competitive mechanism is not established.
entry_context_evidence.source_locator: Author-uploaded full text retained web observation, lines L2429–L2457; JBC279:5537–5548

entry_context_evidence.source_assertion: In MC4100 growth experiments, 300 mM sodium chloride did not induce MG transport and reduced MG-dependent induction by about 50%. This is an induction observation, separate from KM522 salt protection.
entry_context_evidence.source_locator: Author-uploaded full text retained web observation, lines L1251–L1310; JBC279:5537–5548

cdar_qualifier.description: MC4100 reporter/loss-rescue context: active wild-type or pRM1-complemented SdaR/CdaR is inferred from loss in JA176 (paper-numbered P297S) and JA177 (Tn5 20 nt before stop); these mutants are not active endpoints. The paper uses a 391-aa reference versus current P37047 (385 aa); residue numbering is not mapped to the current chain.

evidence.source_assertion: The paper reports a 391-residue yaeG/sdaR reference, JA176 Pro297-to-Ser substitution and JA177 Tn5 insertion 20 nucleotides before the stop codon. These loss mutants inform regulator assignment.

pRM1 contains MC4100 sdaR amplified and cloned in pBluescript; it restores JA176/JA177 growth on glucarate, galactarate and glycerate. Loss and rescue support an activator role, not activation by mutant proteins.

MC4100 sdaR-promoter-lacZ reporters respond to the three inducing carbon sources only with functional SdaR. The source interprets loss of sdaR-lacZ and garP-lacZ activation in knockouts as positive control.
The current issuing P37047 reference is 385 residues; its gene name is cdaR with sdaR and yaeG synonyms. This anchors identity, not equivalence to the paper’s 391-residue sequence numbering.
